prompt: ECMA-262 ForDeclaration BoundNames forbidden string syntax error
answer:
In ECMA-262, the rule

> “It is a Syntax Error if the BoundNames of ForDeclaration contains `let`”

specifically forbids a binding named `let` in a `for-in` or `for-of` `ForDeclaration`.

`let` is singled out because it is not treated as a keyword by the lexical grammar. Instead, in strict mode it is treated as reserved through static-semantic restrictions, including the `ForDeclaration` rule. Thus, `let` is valid in some declaration contexts but forbidden as the bound name in this particular construct.

The same early-error rules also forbid duplicate bound names and conflicts with `VarDeclaredNames` of the loop body. ([Microsoft ECMA-262/6 specification notes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/ie_standards/ms-es6/2faebcb2-1111-1111-badf-ef5ba042fa7f); [Stack Overflow explanation](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/34317632/why-is-let-singled-out-in-the-for-of-specification))
